newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel postpones Zim Navigation public offering.
newsitem.headline: Israel postpones Zim Navigation public offering.

text.p: Israel has decided to postpone the public share offering planned for Zim Israel Navigation Co. Ltd, a government report said.

The annual report of the Government Corporations Authority, in charge of privatisation of government companies, said "the share offering has been postponed at this point due to the drop of profitability of the company and a slump in the capital markets and in the shipping markets."
The government holds 48.6 percent of the company while Israel Corp owns 48.9 percent.
The Government Companies Authority had planned to hold a public share offering of the company in Israel and abroad.
The report also said the government is negotiating with the Israel Corp regarding the further sale of shares of Israel Oil Refineries.

The company is 26 percent held by the Israel Corp and the government owns 74 percent of the shares. The government wants to reach an agreement by which the Israel Corp would give up its right of first refusal for the remaining shares of Oil Refineries. Without this agreement the report said it would be difficult to continue privatisation of the oil refinery.

The report said the net profit of the Government Corporations Authority was 635.5 million shekels in 1995, against a net profit of 94.2 million shekels in 1994 and a loss of 1.2 billion shekels in 1993.

The report said government companies accounted for 2.8 percent of employment in the economy against 3.2 percent in 1994. These companies also accounted for 4.2 percent of Israel's gross domestic product in 1995 against 4.7 percent in 1994.
In 1995 government income from the privatisation was $536 million, against $207.5 million in 1994. In the first five months of 1996 income from privatisation was $181.5 million.
From the start of 1995 to May 1996 the number of government companies fell to 116 from 140.

The most profitable government company was Bezeq Israel Telecom, with a net profit in 1995 of 566 million shekels. The least profitable were Israel Military Industries, with a loss of 341.6 million shekels and Israel Aircraft Industries, with a loss of 156.6 million shekels.
